query: Do Not Drop {A first-year at the top of the shelf ladder is reaching for a bottle labelled, in large letters, DO NOT DROP. It's sliding off their fingertips, over a bench crowded with people.|The same shelf, a different first-year, the same bottle. Someone has added AGAIN to the label.|The bottle is tilting before you've put your bag down. You'd swear it waits for you.} Dive and catch it {You catch it an inch above the bench. Everyone breathes out at once. The first-year comes down the ladder very carefully and shakes your hand for a long time.|Caught, with both hands, against your chest. You put it back on the shelf yourself, at the bottom.|You catch it one-handed without looking, which surprises you more than anyone. Somebody starts a sweepstake on next time.} {You touch it and it skips off your fingers and bursts on the floor. Everyone's eyebrows go blue, yours most.|You get a hand to it and slow it down. It still breaks, but only on your boots, which smoke politely for an hour.|You catch the first-year instead of the bottle. Both of you are blue until Thursday.} Shout everyone back from the bench {"Back!" Everyone backs. The bottle hits the bench and the cloud goes up blue and harmless and smelling of pear drops. The bench is ruined; nobody is.|You clear the bench in a word. The bottle breaks; the first-year cries; the lecturer says it was the right call, in a voice that says it was an expensive one.|You shout before it's fallen. The bench clears; the bottle, perversely, lands upright.} Throw a ward over the bench {The bottle bursts on a pale shell an arm's length above everyone's heads. The cloud rolls off the ward like rain off a window. The first-year, still on the ladder, starts to clap.|A ward, flat over the bench like a tabletop. The bottle breaks on it and the cloud slides off into the sink. The lecturer writes your name down, in the good column.|{spell_level(ward) >= 2: You ward the bench and the first-year at once. Nothing touches anyone. Somebody asks you to teach them; you do, after.|You ward the bench, a little late; the cloud catches your sleeve. Your sleeve is blue. Nobody else is.}}

The Safety Talk
First week, the Great Hall: the safety talk. Sister Amaranth gives it while re-bandaging a prefect. "You will be hexed," she says, "by accident and on purpose. One spell before any other: a ward. It stops one blow." She looks up. "Practise in pairs. Aim low."

results.title: Chalk
results.excerpt:
Chalk
At the top of the lecture tower, where the lamps burn dim on purpose, the umbral lecturer drills first-years in their Ward by throwing chalk. Hard, and without warning. "A ward that only works when you're ready," says the lecturer, "is a decoration."
Hold the ward all hour
